verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four runs are measured before the coolant was ever switched in: case One 'switched 4 May' but 'ran 6 minutes shorter by 29 March', and case Three 'switched 5 October' but 'ran 7 minutes shorter by 30 September'. Those improvements predate the intervention, so half the cases cannot be evidence for it.

The infection rate is computed only over 'the patients discharged from each ward' while 'each ward transferred out a quarter of those admitted', so 25 percent of admitted patients - exactly the group most likely to be transferred because they deteriorated or became infected - is excluded from the denominator and numerator. The 6-11 percent drop is about a narrower population than the claimed 'ward infection rates'.

Revenue per order is measured only on 'the orders that cleared the staffed tills' while 'about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout', so a fifth of orders is missing from a claim about revenue per order overall; a 4-7 percent rise on the staffed-till subset does not establish it for all orders.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: 'Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, and every cohort slept in unconditioned rooms open to outside air', so all four cohorts slept in rooms that got ten degrees colder - itself enough to lower resting heart rate - over exactly the month being compared.
